title: Drawing Letters: How a Typeface Is Born
imageAlt: Type design worktable: pencil sketches of the letter a on grid paper, a laptop showing the a as digital outlines, with violet notes like Start with a pencil, Cap height, Counter, Iterate, Spacing matters and Sketch, construct, refine, digitalize
summary: A hands-on workshop about where letters come from. Starting with pencil, paper and a few simple rules, we’ll look at how a typeface is planned, drawn and refined, then take a handful of letters from first sketch to a digital shape you can type with.
about: Every typeface starts as a set of decisions: how wide, how heavy, how the curves meet the straights. Working the way type designers do, we’ll make those decisions ourselves and see how small choices change the voice of a whole alphabet.
forWho: Designers, illustrators, students and anyone curious about letters, including people who have never drawn one.
levelNote: No lettering or type design experience needed. Bring pencils and patience; everything else is provided.

explore.title: Anatomy of a letter
explore.text: Stems, bowls, counters and serifs: the parts that make a letter readable, and why they look the way they do.

explore.title: Sketching with rules
explore.text: Draw a few key letters, like n, o, H and a, on a simple grid and see how proportion and contrast set the tone of a typeface.

explore.title: From paper to vector
explore.text: Trace your best sketches into clean outlines and learn how curves are built from points and handles.

explore.title: Spacing and rhythm
explore.text: Put letters side by side, adjust the gaps and watch a word start to read as one shape.

outcome: You’ll leave with a small set of your own letters, from first sketch to digital outline, and a sharper eye for the type you see every day.
